root_cause.text: The driver unconditionally invoked the write_read operation for all transfers with a read buffer, including dual/quad reads, where the hardware generates its own clock cycles and transmitting dummy data over shared data lines corrupts the transfer state machine.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that "the core will deal with reads by creating clock cycles itself" and "transmitting garbage data just bricks the transfer since QSPI doesn't have a dedicated master-out line". The patch adds a check for dual/quad modes and routes those transfers to a read-only operation instead of the write_read operation.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 8f9cf02c8852837923f1cdacfcc92e138513325c
Author: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 20 14:28:26 2025 +0100

    spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add regular transfers
    
    The driver for CoreQSPI only supports memory operations at present, so
    add support for regular transfers so that the SD card slot and ADC on
    the BeagleV Fire can be used.
    
    Signed-off-by: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
    Co-developed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The code in mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one unconditionally calls mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op when a transfer has a read buffer (line: 'if (!t->rx_buf) { mchp_coreqspi_write_op(qspi); } else { ... mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op(qspi); }'). The mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op function always transmits dummy data (via 'data = qspi->txbuf ? *((u32 *)qspi->txbuf) : 0xaa;') and uses X4 registers (CONTROL_FLAGSX4) regardless of whether the transfer is a dual or quad read. For dual/quad reads, the hardware generates its own clock cycles and transmitting dummy data over shared data lines corrupts the transfer state machine. The prepare_message function does set up dual/quad modes, but the write_read_op does not differentiate and always performs a write+read, which matches the root cause. No fix (e.g., skipping write for pure dual/quad reads) is present.
